title: HACCP: internal and external documentation—what is the difference?
excerpt: Which documents the team creates itself, and which it keeps in their original form from suppliers and government agencies? Confusing the two is a common source of audit problems.

body.text: Every HACCP plan has two layers of documents. The first contains records created by the operation itself: policies, procedures, journals, and audit reports. The second contains documents received from outside: supplier certificates, safety data sheets for cleaning products, and laboratory reports. Keep them separate: each has its own retention period and role during an inspection.

items: Food-safety policy: a one-page document signed by the manager.
HACCP plan: process diagrams, hazard analysis, CCPs, and their limits.
Kitchen work instructions: handwashing, board labeling, and processing temperatures.
Journals: hygiene, temperature, cleaning, reject products, and training.
Internal audit reports and CAPA records.
Declarations and certificates for raw ingredients and packaging.
Safety data sheets for detergents and disinfectants.
Contractor reports for pest control and service reports for refrigeration equipment.
Laboratory test reports for water and surface swabs.

body.title: A common mistake
body.text: A supplier certificate is filed in the incoming-inspection journal. This makes the records hard to review: an inspector should not have to browse your entries to find a third party’s document.

Keep internal documents in a system that shows the edit history and signatures. Store external documents separately, searchable by supplier and the document’s expiry date. WeSetup separates these workflows: external documents have their own tab and access-control tree.
